Peruvian Hospitality Firm SolAndes Hotels Enters Bankruptcy Proceedings

SolAndes Hotels S.A.C., a prominent player in Peru’s hospitality industry, has entered bankruptcy proceedings, raising concerns about the future of its hotel operations in key destinations including Lima, Cusco, and Arequipa. The company, which operates eight properties under the SolAndes brand, filed for insolvency with the Lima Commercial Court this week, citing “prolonged financial challenges exacerbated by market conditions.”

A statement released by SolAndes management confirmed that the company is now under court-supervised bankruptcy administration. “Our priority remains the well-being of our guests and employees as we navigate this difficult process,” the statement read. “We are committed to maintaining core operations while working towards a restructuring solution.”

As of today, the company has suspended advance bookings for all hotels and closed three properties in Cusco and Arequipa, affecting an estimated 200 rooms. Existing guests at those locations have been offered alternative accommodations at other SolAndes properties or have been assisted in making alternative arrangements. Several restaurants and event spaces managed by SolAndes in Lima have also curtailed services or temporarily closed as a result of the proceedings.

Union representatives expressed concern about the impact on the workforce. “SolAndes employs over 600 hospitality workers nationwide,” said Julio Mendoza, spokesperson for the National Hospitality Workers’ Union. “We are seeking clarity on job security and wage payments for our members during this uncertain period.”

Industry analysts say the bankruptcy filing underscores the persistent volatility facing hospitality operators in Peru. “SolAndes’ situation reflects the ongoing pressures on mid-sized hotel groups in the region,” said Mariela Paredes, a Lima-based hospitality consultant. “Recovery has been uneven, and companies with high fixed costs and debt have struggled to adapt.”

The Peruvian Association of Hospitality Enterprises (APEH) has called for measures to support sector stability. “We urge authorities and stakeholders to work collaboratively to preserve employment and service standards across the industry,” said APEH president Carlos Huaman.

At this stage, SolAndes Hotels’ management has not provided a timeline for the resolution of the bankruptcy process or the potential reopening of shuttered locations. The court-appointed administrator has begun a review of the company’s assets, liabilities, and ongoing obligations. Further operational changes are expected in the coming weeks as the process unfolds.
